laws.rule: Yakushima's mountain area conservation contribution is JPY 1,000 for a day climb and JPY 2,000 if you stay overnight in the mountains (about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026), for secondary-school age and up. It is set by town ordinance but paying is voluntary.
laws.heading: Yakushima mountain area environmental conservation contribution

laws.rule: In Yakushima National Park, feeding wild animals is banned under the Natural Parks Act and a town ordinance, with penalties. From 1 May to 30 September, entry to Nagata beach (a sea-turtle nesting beach) is restricted from 8 pm to 5 am.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Yakushima National Park asks walkers to carry a portable toilet and leave used ones in the trailhead collection boxes, stay on the track and off the mosses, carry all rubbish out, check clothes and bags for seeds, lodge a climbing plan, and pay the mountain conservation contribution. Keep about two car lengths from monkeys and deer, and drive slowly on the Seibu forest road rather than stopping. On turtle beaches use no lights, keep headlights off the sand and join an official observation tour.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Yakushima World Heritage Centre (Ministry of the Environment) and Yakushima Town.
